articles.title: Kevin Harvick Questions RFK’s Brad Keselowski Explanation
articles.summary: Kevin Harvick says RFK Racing's explanation for Brad Keselowski's exit leaves too much unanswered. He also sees few top Cup rides open for the 2012 champion.
articles.body:
Kevin Harvick believes there is more to Brad Keselowski leaving RFK Racing than the team has shared. Harvick discussed the split on this week's episode of SPEED with Harvick and Buxton , the FOX Sports show he co-hosts with Will Buxton.

"So just incredible timing. And I think there's a lot more to this story that we have the pieces to fill in with things that are probably happening off the racetrack and in the race shop. It's too sudden for it not to have more pieces of the puzzle."

RFK Racing and Keselowski announced on Sept. 29 that they will part ways after the season. RFK president Chip Bowers said at Las Vegas on Saturday that the team wanted Keselowski to move into a competition role over the next two to three years.

Bowers compared that role to the jobs held by Chris Gabehart and Chad Knaus . Keselowski wanted to keep driving. MotorBiscuit has more on what Bowers said .

Gabehart was Denny Hamlin's longtime crew chief and later ran competition at Joe Gibbs Racing. He joined Spire Motorsports this year. Knaus won seven titles as Jimmie Johnson's crew chief and remains a Hendrick Motorsports executive.

Harvick said those jobs require an engineering background.

"I don't know how to say this nicely, but I'm going to say it. When you mentioned Chris Gabehart, and you mentioned Chad Knaus, Brad Keselowski is not capable of doing that job."

He praised Keselowski's knowledge as a driver. He said Keselowski can help lead the competition side through feedback and experience.

"But Brad Keselowski is not capable of doing the same things that Chad Knaus and Chris Gabehart are in the same way from a standpoint of engineering and the things that go with that."

Harvick added that the job would be too much to handle while still racing. He agreed with RFK that the role is a full-time commitment.

"He's 100% right. This is a 24-7 job to be able to keep up with the progression that goes with it."

Harvick said the timing makes it hard to find a top Cup ride with five races left in the season. He does not see Keselowski returning to Team Penske , where Austin Cindric drives the No. 2.

He also ruled out Hendrick Motorsports. Connor Zilisch will take over the No. 48 in 2028 when Alex Bowman steps away.

"So I think that the options are very limited for Brad to get back in a winning situation to be able to finish his career, like you'd want to see him finish by winning races."

Harvick did mention Dodge, which is exploring a Cup Series return. Kaulig Racing CEO Chris Rice has said he has not talked with Keselowski, as MotorBiscuit reported last week . Harvick still believes Dodge would be better with Keselowski behind the wheel.

"I think that their Cup car would be better with Brad Keselowski in it."

MotorBiscuit has also looked at possible landing spots for Keselowski . The NASCAR Cup Series races next at Charlotte on Sunday, Oct. 11, as the motorsports world waits on Keselowski's next move.

articles.title: Farmington football forfeits 4 games after playing ineligible players
articles.summary: Farmington self-reported ito the MHSAA after learning two of its players didn’t meet residency requirements.
articles.body:
The Farmington football team has forfeited its first four games because two players who participated in those games were ineligible.

The team is now 1-5 after wins over Ann Arbor Huron and Walled Lake Northern were vacated by the Michigan High School Athletic Association. Its 29-7 win over Livonia Stevenson on Sept. 25 was not impacted by the MHSAA's rulings.

"Farmington Public Schools recently learned that residency information provided to the District for two Farmington High School students was inaccurate and that the students did not meet athletic eligibility requirements," athletic director Allyson Robinson wrote in a statement Thursday, Oct. 8. "Prior to the school year, the District completed the required eligibility process based on the information available at the time. District staff met with the family, reviewed the required residency documentation and confirmed the students' transfer from their previous school.

"When FPS later learned that the residency information provided to the District was inaccurate, we addressed the students' eligibility and self-reported the matter to the MHSAA."

Farmington is in its first season under coach Kason Dickerson, a former assistant who helped Orchard Lake St. Mary's win Division 2 state championships in 2024 and 2025 .

FPS hired Dickerson on March 6 to replace former coach Jason Albrecht, whose teams won two Oakland Activities Association-Blue championships, made three postseason appearances and went 26-23 in five seasons.

This is Dickerson's first head-coaching job. He has spent most of his career as an assistant, coaching defensive backs and working as a passing game coordinator. He also has been part of other winning programs, including West Bloomfield's 2020 state championship team.

Dickerson declined to comment about the forfeitures.

"Eligibility requirements are essential to maintaining fairness and integrity in athletics," Robinson said. "While this outcome is disappointing for our student-athletes and coaches, our focus now is on supporting our football team. These student-athletes have worked hard throughout the season, and we hope they will rally around one another, continue competing, and enjoy the opportunities still ahead of them this season."

articles.title: Warriors predicted to trade Jimmy Butler for $226M explosive duo to revive championship hopes
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors will have some major decisions to make until the trade deadline. In this projection, they part ways with Jimmy Butler.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors are just trying to get as healthy as possible before the regular season, as it is already known that some of their main guys will miss some time. Jimmy Butler is one of those guys.

The veteran went down with a knee injury last season. Butler had to undergo ACL surgery.

"Injured Golden State Warriors star Jimmy Butler underwent successful surgery on his torn right ACL on Monday morning in Los Angeles, the team announced," ESPN's Anthony Slater wrote. "Butler suffered the injury on Jan. 19 in a win over the Miami Heat . He consulted several specialists for the surgery, landing on Dr. Bert Mandelbaum, who performed it on Monday morning with a few members of the Warriors' organization on hand."

In a recent interview, Butler revealed how he was feeling so far into his recovery.

"Great! My knee aches a little bit, but outside of that, I feel amazing. I'm super blessed to be able to play for some amazing organizations with some Hall of Fame players and I can say, I am probably with the greatest player that I have ever played with right now in this team for the greatest organization, so 16 years in and to end up over here with the Warriors, couldn't ask for a better story," Butler said.

With it being unclear how Butler will come back and how real of a shot Golden State has at a championship, Bleacher Report's Greg Swartz proposed a deal that sends him to the New Orleans Pelicans for Trey Murphy III and Dejounte Murray.

"Using Butler's expiring salary, along with a haul of first-round picks, to make a run at Trey Murphy III and Dejounte Murray could help save the Warriors' title hopes and benefit the Pelicans in the long run," Swartz wrote.

This would be a good duo to get for the Warriors, as they are veterans and would provide more depth. Murphy is going to be a hound on the defensive end for the Warriors, and Murray can score the ball.

Murphy and Murray are on the books for $226 million as of right now. Golden State would be taking on two big salaries, but it would be to help Steph Curry chase one last championship. This move could change the complexion of the season for the Warriors.

articles.title: Austin Reaves jokes about paying fans to trash-talk Luka Doncic for one reason
articles.summary: Austin Reaves knows what brings out another level in Luka Doncic, and his playful suggestion gives Lakers fans a glimpse into their partnership.
articles.body:
Austin Reaves has a suggestion for getting the most out of Luka Doncic: Give the Lakers star someone to argue with.An opposing player will do. So might a coach or a fan sitting close enough to be heard. Reaves has seen how Doncic responds when someone challenges him, and he offered a memorable explanation in Chris Mannix's new Sports Illustrated profile .

"I've thought about paying people in the stands to just talk crazy to him," Reaves told Mannix, "because he goes to that different level."

The remark was a playful endorsement of Doncic's competitive streak, rather than an announcement of any actual arrangement. It also revealed something about the relationship between two players central to Los Angeles' hopes: Reaves understands the teammate behind the spectacular scoring performances.

Reaves told Sports Illustrated that Doncic initially kept to himself after arriving from Dallas in the February 2025 trade. Rather than push for an immediate friendship, Reaves let their connection develop naturally.

Now, their time together extends beyond basketball. Mannix reported that Reaves visits the bowling alley at Doncic's Manhattan Beach home, and the two have bonded over golf. Their friendship gives Reaves a close view of the contrast between Doncic's quieter personality away from basketball and his confrontational approach during games. For Reaves, a little outside provocation can bring out the version of Doncic opponents least want to face.

There is a balance to maintain, however. The feature also detailed Doncic's struggles with technical fouls and JJ Redick's efforts to help him keep his competitive intensity from becoming counterproductive.

The Lakers want that edge to produce baskets and wins.

Doncic's Slovenia trip showed another side of his leadership

Doncic's offseason offered a different example of how he can influence the team.

According to Mannix , he hosted Lakers teammates in Ljubljana, Slovenia, for a four-day minicamp in August, covering the costs of a trip that combined pickup basketball with dinners, golf and sightseeing. For a roster with 10 new players following LeBron James' departure, the gathering gave teammates a chance to build connections before the season. Players thanked Doncic with handwritten notes afterward.

That is the broader challenge facing the Lakers star: helping a reshaped team come together while continuing to deliver on the court.

Reaves' joke captures one part of that equation. The Slovenian gathering captures another. Doncic can feed off a challenge from the stands, but the relationships he builds within his own locker room could matter just as much.

articles.title: Ai Tsunoda logra el sexto oro mundial para el judo español
articles.standfirst: La ilerdense suma el primer título para una mujer de nuestro país en 29 años
articles.summary: La ilerdense suma el primer título para una mujer de nuestro país en 29 años
articles.body: El judo español ha sumado hoy en Bakú (Azerbaiyán) el sexto oro mundial de su historia tras la victoria de Ai Tsunoda en la categoría de -70 kilos. La judoca ilerdense derrotó en la final a la austriaca Michaela Polleres, precisamente la rival que le privó del bronce olímpico hace dos años en París. De padre japonés (Go Tsunoda) y madre francesa (Céline Roustant), debutó en este Mundial derrotando a la azerbaiyana Sudaba Aghayeva. Ya en su segundo combate daba buena cuenta de la eslovena Nika Koren, antes de medirse a la neerlandesa y medallista olímpica Sanne van Dijke, que precisamente la había apartado del podio mundial el año pasado en Budapest. Ese tercer triunfo le abría la puerta de la final de su 'pool' ante la sueca Ingrid Nilsson, a la que despachaba para acceder a semifinales. Allí le esperaba la serbia Aleksandra Andrić, de sólo 18 años pero medallista europea en 2025. Tsunoda volvía a salir triunfante con un yuko en el punto de oro (golden score) y se citaba en la final con la austriaca Michaela Polleres, una doble medallista olímpica y mundial que a sus 29 años buscaba su primer gran título internacional. Era la séptima vez que la española y la austriaca se enfrentaban en un tatami, con un balance previo favorable a Tsunoda de 4-2 pese al amargo recuerdo de París 2024. El combate fue muy parejo pero la austriaca recibió finalmente tres Shidos a los tres minutos y 26 segundos del tiempo extra por su falta de competitividad, lo que implica la descalificación inmediata y el triunfo de la oponente por Ippon. El triunfo de esta hija de judocas, de 24 años, supone el sexto oro mundial para el judo español y el primero para una mujer desde el triunfo de Isabel Fernández (-56 kilos) en París 1997. El primero lo había logrado Miriam Blasco, en el mismo peso, en Barcelona 1991. Tsunoda confirma así todo lo bueno que prometía desde sus primeros años, en los que sumó oros mundiales y europeos tanto en la categoría cadete como juvenil, amén del bronce europeo absoluto en Zágreb 2024. España ya había sumado tres medallas en este Mundial gracias a las platas de Ariane Toro (-52) y David García Torné (-66 kilos) y el bronce de Ayumi Leiva, también en -52. Con este oro, España se sitúa segunda en el medallero sólo superada por Japón e iguala los cuatro metales de Budapest 2021, a la espera de que este viernes compita el doble campeón mundial Niko Shera en la categoría de -100 kilos.

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith apologizes to Lane Johnson, Eagles for mental health comments
articles.summary: Stephen A. Smith started ESPN's "First Take" Oct. 8 by apologizing to Lane Johnson and the Philadelphia Eagles for making light of mental health.
articles.body:
ESPN's "First Take" began Thursday, Oct. 8 with a conciliatory note from host Stephen A. Smith, who one day earlier made light of former Philadelphia Eagles offensive lineman Lane Johnson's decision to retire from the NFL while citing a desire to address his mental health and be with his family.

"My intent was joking about the Eagles. Bottom line is this: It doesn't matter what my intent was, it's how it's perceived," said Smith, who walked the comments back on his SiriusXM radio show in the afternoon of Oct. 7 after criticism over his view of the situation became a significant online conversation.

"Here's the reality of the situation: I was wrong. And when you're an adult, and you're a man, you have to admit that you were wrong. I was wrong to Lane Johnson," Smith said. "I was wrong to the Philadelphia Eagles . I messed up because I made light of the issue of mental health," which was not his intent, Smith said.

Smith noted the seriousness of mental health conversations. He commended fellow ESPN employee Kimberly A. Martin, who immediately checked Smith and informed him that his comments were coming off as insensitive.

Smith was concerned that his comments would cause those who struggle with mental health to conceal their hurt rather than seek help.

"There's a lot of people in this country and in this world that are going through mental-health issues. And the biggest regret I have in all of this is the fact that it might have given people that wanted to open the door, to seek help, a reason to pause and hesitate and not do so," Smith said. "And I can't emphasize enough how sorry I am about that, because it is a real issue. And for everybody out there that's struggling, that needs help, please, please, don't look at me as somebody who's trying to dissuade you from doing so. It takes courage for the Lane Johnsons of the world to speak up the way he did ."

With all of the live television he is a part of, Smith said, he will inevitably make mistakes.

"I apologize," Smith said while seated next to moderator Shea Cornette. "I need to do better. And I will."

articles.title: Westcol recibe un golpe de un robot de 90.000 euros en pleno directo y le rompe el set
articles.standfirst: Compró un robot de 90.000 euros para su evento y termina recibiendo un golpe en la cabeza en directo: la insólita escena de Westcol
articles.summary: Compró un robot de 90.000 euros para su evento y termina recibiendo un golpe en la cabeza en directo: la insólita escena de Westcol
articles.body: El mundo de la creación de contenido no deja de sorprender, pero lo ocurrido en la última transmisión del streamer colombiano Westcol ha escalado a un nuevo nivel. En un intento por presumir su más reciente y costosa adquisición tecnológica, el creador de contenido terminó siendo víctima de un golpe en directo propinado por su propio robot humanoide. El incidente ocurrió durante un stream en la plataforma Kick. Westcol presentaba a su audiencia un robot de 1,70 metros de altura, cuyo valor asciende a unos 90.000 euros (aproximadamente 98.000 dólares). Para mostrar las avanzadas capacidades del autómata, el streamer, acompañado por el cantante y productor colombiano Blessd, decidió poner música para ver si la máquina era capaz de seguir el ritmo. Sin embargo, el ambiente festivo cambió de manera repentina. Al sonar la música, el androide se activó automáticamente y comenzó a mover los brazos, conectándole un golpe directo en la parte trasera de la cabeza a Westcol, quien se encontraba de espaldas justo delante de él. A pesar de lo aparatoso del impacto, el streamer no sufrió heridas de gravedad y pudo continuar con la emisión. El puñetazo no fue el único contratiempo de la jornada. En la misma transmisión, el autómata lanzó una patada involuntaria hacia una de las estanterías de la habitación, rompiendo en pedazos una vitrina de cristal. La combinación de estos accidentes llevó a miles de usuarios a calificar el directo como una escena sacada de un episodio de la conocida serie futurista Black Mirror. El momento no tardó en volverse viral en redes sociales, generando la reacción de referentes de la comunidad hispanohablante como Ibai Llanos y TheGrefg, quienes calificaron el metraje como uno de los mejores clips del año. A pesar de las complicaciones del directo, la compra del autómata tiene un propósito muy claro. El dispositivo no fue adquirido simplemente como entretenimiento personal, sino que será una de las atracciones principales de Stream Fighters 5. El evento, programado para el próximo 14 de noviembre en el Coliseo MedPlus de Bogotá, albergará un inédito combate donde se enfrentarán los robots de Westcol y Blessd. Tras lo visto en el stream, la expectativa por ver cómo se comportarán estas máquinas en el ring ha aumentado significativamente entre los fanáticos del espectáculo digital.

articles.title: La picante confesión de Camilo Cifuentes sobre su infidelidad a Westcol y Blessd: "La cagué"
articles.standfirst: El influencer contó en directo su error con su ex pareja y cómo se enamoró de La Mijita
articles.summary: El influencer contó en directo su error con su ex pareja y cómo se enamoró de La Mijita
articles.body: El escándalo en torno a Camilo Cifuentes, conocido por su contenido en redes sociales y sus causas benéficas, alcanzó su punto máximo tras una transmisión en vivo en la plataforma Kick. En el espacio compartido junto al streamer Westcol y el cantante urbano Blessd, Cifuentes abordó de manera abierta la polémica de infidelidad en la que se vio envuelto tras la filtración de chats y fotografías privadas. Durante más de una hora de transmisión, Cifuentes admitió no haber sido sincero con las dos mujeres involucradas: su expareja María Camila Sepúlveda —quien actualmente se encuentra embarazada de su primer hijo— y la influencer Anthía López, conocida como 'La Mijita'. "Yo soy Camilo Cifuentes y yo la cagué (...). Yo no fui sincero al hacer las cosas. No le fui sincero a 'La Mijita', ella no sabía que yo hablaba con la mamá de mi hijo. Yo le dije que nos habíamos dejado, pero hablaba con la mamá de mi hijo diciéndole que quería formar un hogar con ella", reconoció el influencer. A pesar de admitir la falta de transparencia, Cifuentes sorprendió al afirmar que no se arrepentía de lo vivido: "Yo no me arrepiento, para mí no fue un error". Explicó que la falla residió en el manejo de la situación y la falta de honestidad, no en los sentimientos o experiencias compartidas. Asimismo, aclaró que 'La Mijita' no tenía conocimiento completo de la situación y pidió a la audiencia que cesaran los ataques hacia ambas mujeres, confirmando además que su intención es continuar su relación sentimental con López. La transmisión, que llegó a situar el nombre de Camilo Cifuentes en el primer lugar de tendencias de X (anteriormente Twitter) en Colombia, contó con las intervenciones del cantante Blessd y de Westcol. Blessd instó al creador de contenido a asumir el error ante la opinión pública pero sin dejarse derrumbar por las críticas en redes sociales: "Usted lo que tiene que decir es: 'Tuve un error, sí me equivoqué... y a aquella le pido disculpas y a la otra también'. A la gente que no le gustó lo que hice, piensen lo que quieran, que yo soy humano también", le sugirió el artista urbano, enfatizando en que lo más primordial es velar por el bienestar del futuro bebé. Por su parte, Westcol contextualizó la situación dentro de las dinámicas del mundo del entretenimiento digital: "Bienvenido al mundo de la celebridad, bienvenido a la gente del internet. Lo único que usted tiene que hacer es seguir siendo la misma persona y luchar por lo que sueña", expresó el streamer, calificando el gesto de dar la cara públicamente como un acto de madurez. Camilo Cifuentes confesó también cómo se fue enamorando de la influencer La Mijita: “Ella y yo teníamos una amistad, yo la admiraba a ella por todo lo que hizo en el terremoto y ella a mí porque me acompañó a Buenaventura a repartir mercados Yo nunca había conocido a una mujer tan trabajadora como La Mijita, ella es demasiado”. Al mismo tiempo contó que cuando empezó el romance, ella tenía también una pareja, pero siempre fue respetuosa con la verdad: “Con el tiempo no empezamos a encariñar, pero es que ella también tenía pareja, en ese momento, pero ella siempre fue una dama, siempre respetuosa, siempre que viajábamos fue respetuosa, porque ella tenía pareja, pero lo de ella se acabó por cosas que tiene el destino. Ella siempre fue muy sincera, yo fui el que no fui sincero” Pese al impacto mediático de la controversia, Camilo Cifuentes aseguró estar dispuesto a afrontar las consecuencias profesionales o pérdidas económicas que esto le pueda acarrear, incluyendo el cierre de sus perfiles digitales o la pérdida de patrocinadores. No obstante, remarcó la importancia de mantener sus ingresos, dado que de su trabajo dependen económicamente varios familiares, un equipo de trabajo y las obligaciones futuras con su hijo. «Mi mayor sueño es tener un hijo que crezca en un hogar, pero si no lo podemos formalizar, ser el mejor papá del mundo», concluyó, comprometiéndose a garantizar el sustento económico tanto de su hijo como de la madre.

articles.title: Man City charges: Haaland says Premier League club must ‘stick together’
articles.summary: Erling Haaland calls on Manchester City to unite as Premier League club appeals more than 100 charges of wrongdoing.
articles.body:
Manchester City striker Erling Haaland says the Premier League club must ‘stick together’ following the guilty verdict delivered on more than 100 charges for financial breaches.

The league leaders head to Liverpool on Sunday ⁠⁠for their first game since an independent commission found the club guilty of serious breaches of Premier League financial rules over nine years, as well as charges relating to their failure to co-operate with the investigation.

City have insisted they are innocent of all charges and have appealed the decision. Should the verdict be upheld, City could face relegation, points deductions and fines.

“We are going to have a good time [on Sunday]. We have to stick together, we have to stay positive. We have to look ahead and try to win football games,” Haaland told the United Kingdom broadcaster Sky Sports.

“No matter what happens in life we always have to have a smile.”

“We have to enjoy the situation. We have to spread the love to each other, stick together, enjoy the ride and smile.”

Haaland welcomes Liverpool test for Manchester City

City have won all five of their matches in the Premier League this season and are three points clear of last season’s champions, Arsenal.

Liverpool are sixth in the league and six points behind City, after a mixed start for their new manager Andoni Iraola. The joint record Premier League winners, with 20 titles alongside Manchester United, are, however, undefeated.

The Reds will also be buoyed by what is expected to be an even more vociferous support than usual at their Anfield home.

During the period that Manchester City were investigated, 2009-2018, Liverpool finished second by two points behind City.

Under the management of Jurgen Klopp, they also twice finished just a point behind Pep Guardiola’s City in subsequent years.

The allegation from rival fans is that City’s financial wrongdoing was tantamount to cheating and gave the club a significant advantage during that time and the seasons that have followed the period in question.

With that, Anfield is expected to deliver an angry and hostile reception for the current City squad, but Haaland, who played with Molde, Salzburg and Borussia Dortmund before joining City, says the game itself is always a big occasion.

“It is always special to play against Liverpool,” Haaland continued.

“Especially with Pep and Klopp, I remember sitting in Molde, Salzburg and Dortmund watching the games and how much they pushed each other.

“It is always special to play a game there. Every game against Liverpool is special.”

What does the future hold for Haaland and Man City?

Haaland was born in England, while his father – Alf-Inge Haaland – was a player in the Premier League for City and Leeds United.

The 26-year-old Norwegian international has, alongside the majority of City’s squad, been heavily linked with a move away from the club, should they be relegated.

In the meantime, Haaland was keen to stress what the club means to him and his family.

“I care a lot about this place. I spent my first four years here. It is a special place for us [his family],” Haaland added.

“I care a lot about City and the fans, I am a fan myself and I feel with them.”

articles.title: Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz says freshman Johnnie ‘DJ’ Jones receives a heart transplant
articles.summary: Missouri freshman offensive tackle Johnnie “DJ” Jones has received a heart transplant, coach Eli Drinkwitz said.
articles.body: Missouri freshman offensive tackle Johnnie “DJ” Jones has received a heart transplant, coach Eli Drinkwitz said. Drinkwitz announced on X on Thursday morning that the surgery Wednesday went well and that Jones was recovering. “We are incredibly grateful for the medical team who cared for DJ and for the donor and donor family whose extraordinary gift made this possible,” Drinkwitz wrote. Drinkwitz said at a news conference Tuesday that Jones was hospitalized at the Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville, Florida, where he was awaiting the transplant. Missouri staff first found an issue with Jones’ heart over the summer during freshman intake testing, Drinkwitz said earlier this week. The team’s medical staff sought a second opinion with the Mayo Clinic when they weren’t getting a resolution or answers after two weeks of observation. Doctors at the Mayo Clinic detected a much more serious heart problem, Drinkwitz said. The coaching staff was told last week that Jones needed the transplant. The 18-year-old Jones graduated from Venice High School on Florida’s Gulf Coast and signed with Missouri as a four-star recruit.

articles.title: Senegal-Morocco AFCON title decision within days, says CAS
articles.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport to rule within days on appeal against decision to strip Senegal of AFCON title.
articles.body:
A speedy resolution to Senegal’s appeal after being stripped of the Africa Cup ⁠of Nations (AFCON) title has ⁠been promised by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), who heard arguments on Thursday and said it will have a decision in days.

Senegal are contesting the Confederation of African Football’s (CAF) ⁠decision to declare Morocco champions, despite Senegal beating the hosts 1-0 after extra time in January’s final in Rabat.

Senegal walked off the pitch for 14 minutes after a penalty was awarded against them late ⁠in regulation time, with several players returning to the dressing room in protest before they resumed play.

Morocco failed to convert the spot kick, sending the match into extra time, where Senegal scored the winner to secure victory.

However, they were stripped of the title two months later after CAF’s Appeal Board ruled that Senegal ‌had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch, overturning the result and awarding a 3-0 victory to Morocco .

Senegal quickly followed with an appeal to sport’s highest court, CAS, which was lodged on March 25 but heard on Thursday .

“I know it’s a long wait for the fans a few months after the final between Senegal and Morocco,” said CAS Director General Matthieu Reeb.

“The timetable and the procedural calendar were established with the agreement of the parties involved in this case. So ⁠everybody knew about the timeline, and our objective as CAS, as the ⁠last instance authority, is to provide a reasoned award as soon as possible after the hearing today,” he told reporters.

The long-running saga over the winner of this year’s Africa Cup of Nations title will be concluded within days, although Reeb did not ⁠give a definite date.

“I expect the decision to come not today, not tomorrow, but a few days later. The facts are set, are clear, and ⁠the discussions will be on some procedural issues and legal ⁠aspects,” he added.

The CAS panel, presided over by French sports law expert Gerald Simon with assistance from Italian international law professor Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based lawyer and professor of law at the University of Zurich Ulrich Haas, heard the pleadings of the parties ‌who were represented by their lawyers, with the hearing completed on Thursday.

Morocco’s delegation did not speak to the media. Senegal General Secretary Abdoulaye Sow said they were confident.

“But the important thing is that sports law ‌is ‌upheld, and that this particular match is put to bed, for the sake of dignity and for Africa,” Sow told reporters outside the hearing, which was held behind closed doors.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark says she blocks social media hate and enjoys hostile WNBA road crowds
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark condemned racist rhetoric and discrimination while revealing she can't remember the last time she read a direct message on social media.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark said she can't remember the last time she read a direct message on social media. She also enjoys getting booed by opposing fans. Apparently, WNBA players can be the subject of an enormous amount of attention without volunteering to spend their entire day focusing on the worst aspects of it. CAITLIN CLARK'S LOWEST-RATED PLAYOFF GAME STILL OUTDREW EVERY NON-FEVER FIRST-ROUND BROADCAST During her season-ending news conference Thursday, Clark condemned "racist rhetoric" and "discrimination," praised passionate crowds and explained how she tries to manage the noise surrounding her. It was a refreshingly sane approach to a subject that has produced far too much nonsense around the WNBA. Some players, and plenty of people covering them, should take notice. The discussion began with a question about Kelsey Mitchell's comments on the attention that comes with being Clark's teammate. Clark said seeing teammates go through that upset her. She rejected people using her name to promote racism or discrimination. "That's never been something I've stood for," Clark said. "For those of you that know me, that's not what I'm about. It's not how I was raised." While Clark acknowledged that people shouldn't be sending nasty messages on social media, she said she tries to avoid reading them. "I couldn't tell you the last time I read a direct message," Clark said. "I just try to block out the noise the best I can." There is a useful lesson in that. Condemning someone else's behavior doesn't require giving that person unlimited access to your attention. Online trolls seek attention, which is why they send vile messages in the first place. Spending your time thinking about and reacting to those comments gives the trolls exactly what they want. Caitlin Clark welcomes the boos Clark recalled Golden State fans booing her every time she touched the ball. "I like that. I thought that was great and fun," she said. Imagine that. A professional athlete enjoying an opposing crowd trying to throw her off her game. "You can boo. You can yell at people," Clark said. She even brought up watching the Yankees in the playoffs. "Man, those Yankee fans are brutal," she said with a smile. Anyone expecting a visiting star to receive a warm welcome in every building should probably spend a little more time watching sports. Those fans want to see their team win, and opponents are just standing in the way. The atmosphere is part of what makes a road win satisfying. Enjoying it doesn't mean accepting everything fans say or do, as Clark made clear. "I think there's certainly a line and that can't be crossed," she said, adding that "there's certain rhetoric that's just not okay." Where that line falls became a major subject of debate during the playoffs, when Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson confronted a Fever fan. "You don’t step towards me. You never should step and point at me," Wilson said afterward. Prime Video's broadcasters defended Wilson without knowing what the fan had said. Apparently, her reaction was all the evidence they needed. But as OutKick reported, both the Fever and WNBA found no fan-conduct violation. DAN DAKICH BLASTS A'JA WILSON OVER FAN INCIDENT IN PLAYOFF LOSS TO THE FEVER Clark was discussing her own experiences Thursday. Still, her willingness to enjoy a hostile road crowd offers a useful perspective in a league where interactions with spectators have become such a consuming subject. This wasn't the first time an opposing player accused a Fever fan of inappropriate conduct despite the team and league finding no such evidence. Fever general manager Amber Cox said no fans had been removed for misconduct at home this season. Yet, left-wing podcaster Sarah Spain said Cox was being "defensive." Well, wouldn't you be defensive if people kept trashing your fans and you had information that contradicted what they were saying? WNBA could use more focus on the positive Clark's answer showed how easily a person can condemn misconduct while also expressing appreciation for fans. Those positions fit together just fine. "For the real fans that do show up and do support and do respect, I applaud you," she said. "And there are a lot of you. And that's not just here in Indianapolis. That's across the league." When every conversation about fans revolves around the worst behavior, or the alleged worst behavior, the people who show up, support their teams and make the games worth watching can disappear from the discussion. The rest of the WNBA would benefit from spending a little more time focusing on those people and a little less time reading DMs.

articles.title: Kentucky getting a visit from Louisiana pass rusher
articles.summary: Kentucky football is always in recruiting mode, and will host a 2028 pass rusher from Louisiana this weekend.
articles.body:
Kentucky football target Hayden Monroe has loved the LSU Tigers the way most Louisiana boys do, without being asked and with no plan to stop. On Saturday he goes to Lexington to watch the Bayou Bengals play someone else. That someone else would like very much to have him.

Monroe is a 2028 athlete at Carencro who has played both sides of the ball and has never been caught apologizing for either. As a junior he has 37 tackles, six sacks, seven tackles for loss, and a forced fumble. He also has 12 quarterback hurries, which leads Louisiana. Sacks go in the newspaper. Hurries go in the film room, where coaches keep the things they truly believe.

That is why the phone rings. It rings from Lexington, and it rings from other places too.

"I'm really looking forward to experiencing an SEC game day and seeing the atmosphere at Kentucky," Monroe said. "LSU is a team I grew up watching and loving, so getting to be there for that matchup makes it even more special. But Kentucky has really made me feel wanted throughout this process, and I'm excited to get around the coaches, see the program up close, and experience everything for myself."

The order of those sentences is worth noticing. LSU gets the first mention and Kentucky gets the last word. A recruit does not volunteer that he feels wanted unless somebody has gone to the trouble of making him feel it.

Somebody has. Ethan Workman, Steve Gillette and Tony Washington have done much of the dialing, a three-man rotation in the oldest business in college football, which is persistence. Monroe has taken note.

"Kentucky has definitely been standing out with the way they've been recruiting me," he said.

He has also watched the Wildcats play, and he did not need subtitles.

"I like the way they play defense and how physical they are," Monroe said. "I feel like my versatility as an edge guy would fit what they're building. I've also noticed they have guys from Louisiana on the roster, so that stands out to me because it shows they're comfortable recruiting players from back home and those guys can come up there and fit in. I'm excited to learn more about how they see me in their defense."

That second observation is the sort a recruit makes quietly and files away. Nobody wants to be the first Louisianan to make the drive north and find out the hard way whether anyone saved him a seat. Monroe has counted the heads already. He knows he would not be alone.

He is not exactly short of company on the call sheet, either. Cincinnati, by his account, phones him every day, and Tulane and Houston have shown him what he calls a lot of love. He does not sound like a young man in any hurry to choose.

"I'm keeping everything open right now and just continuing to build relationships," he said.

That is the right answer, and it is the one every program in the chase would rather not hear.

So Kentucky will have its chance Saturday, with a full house, a rival he grew up cheering for and the three men who have been working the phones now standing in front of him. A visit is only a long look, and it cuts both ways. The program gets to show the boy what it is. The boy gets to decide whether he believes it.

For one afternoon, the Bayou will sit in the Bluegrass and watch what happens. What Monroe sees is his own business. Kentucky has done what it could to make it worth the drive.
authors: Lee Ann Herring Olvedo, UK Wildcats Wire

articles.title: 115-Year-Old ‘Holy Grail’ Baseball Card Goes for Auction with Estimated Value of $3 Million or More
articles.summary: The T206 Honus Wagner baseball card has sold at auction in the past for more than $6 million, making it one of the most valuable sports cards of all time
articles.body:
One of the rarest baseball cards in history is currently up for auction with an estimated value of $3 million

The card — a T206 Honus Wagner — features the late Pittsburgh Pirates shortstop, who died in 1996 at 81

The card was manufactured between 1909 and 1911 and distributed in cigarette packs before being pulled from production; copies of it have sold at auction for more than $6 million in the past

One of the rarest baseball cards in history — a T206 Honus Wagner — is currently up for auction, and it's estimated to fetch a price of $3 million or more.

At least 115 years old, the card features late Pittsburgh Pirates shortstop Honus Wagner and is up for auction through Heritage Auctions . According to the listing, it has been authenticated by Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) and has a value of over $3 million. The current bid on Thursday, Oct. 8, is nearing $1 million.

Known as the T206 Honus Wagner, or "Connecticut Wagner," the card was produced by the American Tobacco Company between 1909 and 1911 and distributed inside cigarette packs before being pulled from production.

Only 53 verified copies of the card are known to exist, according to The Athletic . Of those, 10 were graded a PSA 1 grading, meaning that they are determined to be in "Poor" condition.

Thanks to the card's rarity, it's been referred to as the "Holy Grail of all trading cards" by PSA on its website.

Exactly why the card is so rare has never been confirmed. One theory, according to PSA, is that Wagner, who died in 1995 at age 81, objected to profiting from his likeness. Another theory is that he did not want his name associated with tobacco products.

Regardless, the scarcity of the card has made the T206 Honus Wagner one of the most valuable pieces of sports memorabilia in history.

On Aug. 16, 2021, one of the cards sold for $6.606 million, setting a record for the most expensive sports card ever purchased, per USA Today . That record stood until August 2025 , when a 2007–08 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Dual Logoman Autograph card featuring Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant sold for $12.932 million through Heritage Auctions.

In February, The Athletic reported that a PSA-graded 1 T206 Honus Wagner card sold for $5.1 million.

According to the outlet, the card was passed down to brothers Dennis and Douglas Shields, who inherited it from their grandfather Morton Bernstein. Bernstein pulled the card from a cigarette pack while working at a silver manufacturing plant and started collecting trading cards in the early 1900s.

"My brother and I have held on to these for years," Dennis told the outlet. "It isn't for monetary issue; but it was the sentimental value that our grandfather held on to these things all his life, and we held on to them just because we love him."

After more than a century in the family, the brothers ultimately put the card up for sale through Goldin Auctions.

"I've never been able to trace a Wagner that has stayed in only one family since the day the card came out," Ken Goldin, CEO and founder of Goldin Auctions, told the outlet at the time. "The (Shieldses') care and respect for their grandfather's collection — carefully looked after behind closed doors for 116 years — has preserved one of the hobby's true grails, and the importance of this cannot be overstated."

Michael King, Case Mize, Robbie Ray, and Nick Pivetta are all set to hit the open market, so long as King opts out of his $58 million contract this offseason. But even if he does, the Padres can bring him back on a new multi-year deal.

Bleacher Report's Joel Reuter is predicting that the Padres will re-sign King this offseason in what should be an obvious outcome following his postseason heroics for San Diego this year.

Padres predicted to make obvious decision and re-sign Michael King

"King can opt out of his final two years and $58 million of his contract this winter. He almost certainly will since he would immediately slot in as the No. 2 starter on the market behind Tarik Skubal," Reuter writes.

With a really good chance for King to land a massive contract this offseason, King seems like a lock to hit the open market by opting out of his current contract.

For the Padres, this presents a bit of a problem. If he hits free agency, which looks likely, he'll have a real chance to land a massive contract from another contender.

But there should not be any question for the Padres this offseason. As Reuter predicts, the Padres should re-sign King this winter, which would be an obvious outcome following his heroics in the postseason.

In three games in the postseason this year, one of which was a relief appearance on one day's rest after a Game 2 start, King had a 0.64 ERA with one win, one save, and 15 strikeouts in 14 innings of work.

The veteran right-hander had a 3.21 ERA during the regular season, in which he posted 4.3 bWAR, the best mark of his MLB career so far.

King will be 32 years old next season, and as Kerry Miller of Bleacher Report predicted, King "should have no problem whatsoever fetching nine figures on a five-year deal."

That means $100 million over five years is the minimum for King in Miller's mind, which, all things considered, wouldn't be a bad deal for the Padres; that's how good King was this year.

After an impressive postseason performance for the Padres, signing King to a long-term deal is an obvious decision the Padres should make. Reuter is predicting that's exactly what will happen, as he's predicting King re-signs with the Padres this offseason.

articles.title: £29m star confirms he will replace club legend at Liverpool
articles.summary: An exciting player is coming to replace a club legend at Liverpool. Jurgen Klopp's departure confirmed that it was the end of an era at Anfield. The German l...
articles.body:
An exciting player is coming to replace a club legend at Liverpool.

Jurgen Klopp's departure confirmed that it was the end of an era at Anfield. The German left the club more than two years ago now and the team that is now lining up under Andoni Iraola looks markedly different.

There's no Mo Salah, no Trent Alexander-Arnold nor even Luis Diaz and Darwin Nunez. The future Klopp envisioned for the Reds is now being spearheaded by the likes of Florian Wirtz and Jeremy Jacquet.

It has been orchestrated by Richard Hughes, who has not been short of criticism and who has also departed the club for pastures new.

But the change that has undergone is only the beginning. There will be more on the way very soon.

Why two club legends will leave Liverpool in 2027

This summer we saw Salah and Andy Robertson depart. They were the linchpins of the Klopp era who were integral to the success of the team.

Both will go down as two of the greatest to ever play for the club. Salah in particular was basically a King in Merseyside. The Egyptian King so to speak - an ethereal deity who felt superhuman most of the time.

But next summer could be an even bigger foundational change.

Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker are yet to extend their contracts that expire at the end of the season. At this stage both are going to be leaving the club.

Given their ages, it is unlikely they will be extending any further.

Giorgi Mamardashvili confirms he's coming to replace Alisson

When the Georgian was signed for £29m in 2024 it became very obvious that he would be coming to take over from Alisson in the future.

However, Mamardashvili's shaky performances in a Liverpool shirt so far combined with the acquisition of Lucca Brughmans have raised some questions.

But Mamardashvili confirmed he is the man to replace Liverpool's club legend. During the international break he was in inspired form, often keeping his country in the games that they played.

Mamardashvili's stunning performance against Northern Ireland, where he made several key saves and stopped a penalty as well was the icing on the cake - the performance that confirmed he is world-class and that he is ready to be coming in to replace Alisson.

Iraola is also a fan. He wanted to sign Mamardashvili while he was at Bournemouth. So, the matter is settled.

articles.title: 7 best and worst fantasy football matchups for Week 5
articles.summary: Four players have great Week 5 fantasy football matchups, while several others should be parked on your bench. How should we handle D'Andre Swift?
articles.body:
C.J. Stroud threw for 347 yards and Jameson Williams finally hit the century mark in a 2026 game. Last week was arguably our most accurate fantasy football matchups column yet, and I expect the overall hit rate to improve each week as we gain more data and insights on team and player tendencies.

Every week, I'll continue to identify and write up players that are not obviously starts or sits. Regardless of matchup, you're starting someone like James Cook every week, so I try to go a few layers deeper than your early-round fantasy studs.

Note: Projections refer to player props in the betting and prediction markets, which are a valuable reference tool for anyone playing fantasy football.

Fantasy football Week 5 start ’em, sit ’em: Players to start and bench

Quarterbacks are averaging 327 passing yards, three passing touchdowns, and 29 fantasy points per game against Detroit this season. Even when adjusting for opponents faced (Tyler Shough, Josh Allen, Geno Smith and Bryce Young), the Lions have still allowed more than six fantasy points per game to the position above expectation.

The game total in Cardinals-Lions is a hearty 54.5 points, the highest of Week 5. Brissett himself has attempted at least 35 passes in three of four games, and he's averaging the eighth-most pass attempts per game (38) overall. Almost the entire Lions secondary is injured, as cornerback Rock Ya-Sin is set to miss Week 5, making him the fourth Lions starter to go down in their secondary.

Think of Brissett as a top-10 fantasy option this week, much like Stroud last week against the Cowboys.

Let's address the elephant in the room. Yes, D'Andre Swift was benched last week after a bad fumble. Kyle Monangai looked like superman in relief, carrying 30 times for 146 yards and two scores. Monangai himself is now a little banged up, and I expect Week 5 to be the D'Andre Swift show once again.

Swift signed a lucrative three-year extension with the Bears before the season began, and Head Coach Ben Johnson appears to have already moved on from the fumble. In a presser post-game, Johnson stated :

"I think the [fumble] last week was egregious... and [Swift] knows that. He takes a lot of pride in [not fumbling], hence why it's never been an issue over the course of his career... he'll be just fine moving forward."

The Bears head coach is ready to move on, and so are we. Green Bay has allowed 114 rushing yards and nearly two touchdowns per game to running backs on the ground this season. When adjusting for opponents faced, the Packers are sneakily the #1 matchup to target for our fantasy backs.

Vegas isn't worried about Swift either, as sportsbooks have his total yards projected for 78.5, with roughly 50-50 odds to score.

The Commanders have been a unique case study in how pass defenses funnel production. Through four weeks, the Commanders have given up nearly eight times as many yards to receivers on the outside compared to the slot. This is by far the biggest ratio among any NFL defense this year.

Nabers himself has run 80% of his routes on the outside, and he's coming off a big six-catch, 112-yard game with a touchdown.

The Commanders have also held two of their four opponents to under 40 rushing yards, and with Cam Skattebo (shoulder) limited in practice this week, there's a decent chance the Giants are forced to work through the air to attack Washington's defense.

Nabers continues to be a polarizing fantasy asset, but I'm giving you the green light to start him again in an excellent matchup.

The rookie broke out in Week 3 with seven catches, 105 yards and a touchdown. And then Week 4 was radio silence (kind of).

For those hurt by Sadiq's Week 4 donut, it's time to get back on the horse once again. While Sadiq failed to bring in any of his four targets, Geno Smith only attempted 15 passes last week. So, Sadiq's four targets actually tied with Garrett Wilson for a team-leading 27% target share.

Diving deeper, Sadiq only ran 12 routes, so he was being targeted on an unreal 1 in 3 routes. Many are saying (okay, maybe just me) that this was the quietest force-feeding of targets for any player through four weeks.

Turning to the matchup, the Browns have allowed a 27% target share to tight ends this year, a top-10 mark. It becomes even more favorable when you look at the mixed bag of opponents the Browns have faced (Brenton Strange, Cade Otton, Darren Waller, Pat Freiermuth, Darnell Washington).

Take the plunge with me and trust Sadiq as an upside play in Week 5 given the matchup.

25 best fantasy football running back PPR seasons since 2001

The Falcons pressured Shough on nearly half his dropbacks last week, and it ended up being his worst fantasy output by far of the young 2026 campaign. This week, Shough faces the Vikings, who are undefeated almost entirely due to their defense.

No team has pressured quarterbacks at a higher rate than the Vikings, and they've held opposing quarterbacks to just 12.5 fantasy points per game. It's also a short week for the Saints after their Monday night trouncing at the hands of Atlanta.

Shough should be treated like a fringe top-12 option in fantasy, where the aforementioned Brissett is a better Week 5 option.

Tony Pollard has put together a nice string of fantasy performances, with 13 fantasy points in back-to-back weeks. Unfortunately, that likely ends this week against Houston.

The Texans are holding running backs to just 3.55 yards per carry, despite facing Jonathan Taylor and James Cook already. Both those star backs were held to under 70 rushing yards. Overall, the Texans are the third-worst matchup for fantasy backs when adjusting each defense for opponents faced.

There is also a massive discrepancy between the Texans defensive line (Will Anderson, Danielle Hunter) and a downright bad Titans offensive line. Betting and prediction markets peg Pollard's touchdown odds at less than 29%, an impressively low number for a starting NFL running back.

Park Pollard on your fantasy bench this week.

Every Eagles Player at the Jaguars (London game)

It's been about as bad of a four-game runout as anyone could possibly imagine for the Eagles .

Superstar guard Landon Dickerson is on injured reserve

Saquon Barkley should miss this game due to a hamstring injury

DeVonta Smith should miss this game due to a hamstring injury

Tank Bigsby is now on Injured Reserve for core muscle surgery

Dallas Goedert is hoping to return from a sprained MCL in Week 2

When the bullet points emerge, you know it's bad news, but the hits keep coming. This week, the Eagles face a Jaguars team that has allowed the fewest rushing yards per game to running backs (48). Jacksonville has also allowed just three passing touchdowns on the season, the lowest mark through four games.

Jalen Hurts' pass yards prop is under 190, it's just a complete mess. The Eagles are more than touchdown underdogs in a low 41.5 point game total.

It's also a London game, which is really just another home game for the Jaguars, who have played more than twice as many games there as any other NFL franchise. Like Tampa Bay last week, this is not a week to fire up any Eagles in fantasy football.

articles.title: How Pelicans’ Jeremiah Fears is being challenged in a totally different way to level up defense
articles.summary: The New Orleans Pelicans spent years watching defensive possessions unravel because of missed assignments, late rotations, and breakdowns that leave everyone...
articles.body:
The New Orleans Pelicans spent years watching defensive possessions unravel because of missed assignments, late rotations, and breakdowns that leave everyone scrambling. New head coach Jamahl Mosley is determined to eliminate those mistakes, but his approach demands a different understanding of the game, particularly from Jeremiah Fears.

Thankfully, though the defensive drills keep coming with Mosley in charge of the Pelicans , and Fears keeps learning. For the second-year point guard, the arrival of a new head coach has meant a complete rewiring of how the 19-year-old thinks about defense. And, as Fears shared during Media Day , the learning curve is very steep.

"It's very different," Fears admitted to ClutchPoints. "Obviously there are so many things that you can learn from coach and his defensive scheme, and I think it helps. It just helped the overall team, us being able to understand positions and understand you don't always have the ball. Like you said, you may be the low man sometimes, and you've got to understand your job and what the team needs you to do in the moment or in that moment."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The challenge is not necessarily about playing harder. Fears has already demonstrated the competitive streak and fearlessness that helped make him one of the league's most intriguing young prospects. What Mosley wants now is a more disciplined defender who understands where to be, when to help, and how his positioning affects the other four players on the floor.

That distinction represents a significant adjustment for Fears, who averaged 14.3 points, 3.7 rebounds, 3.4 assists, and 1.2 steals while appearing in all 82 games as a rookie. The former Oklahoma standout showed he could handle substantial offensive responsibilities despite being one of the NBA's youngest players. His second season, however, will require a different kind of growth.

"So just being able to make sure we all know what we are doing on the floor. Sometimes you don't pick the ball up. Maybe your teammate picks the ball up, but you got to be in the gap," explained Fears. "You got to be in that for him. So it's just understanding that and just continuing to learn. You don't always know everything. Continue to ask questions, continue to watch film, and like I said, the more you learn, the better you'll be."

Perhaps the most encouraging training camp development is that Fears appears receptive to the challenge. Rather than suggesting he already understands the nuances of Mosley's system, he acknowledged the importance of asking questions and accepting that there is more to learn.

His rookie season established Fears as a legitimate building block for the franchise's future. His sophomore campaign offers an opportunity to prove his development will not be limited to scoring and playmaking.

If that lesson takes hold, the Pelicans could have something considerably more valuable than another young guard capable of filling up the box score. Those are a dime a dozen at this level; just check the G League. If Fears steps up on defense, then New Orleans will finally have a spiritual successor to Chris Paul at point. If nothing else goes right this season, knowing that piece is in place moving forward would go a long way toward winning back fans and games sooner rather than later.

articles.title: Saints renew a mostly torturous series history against the Vikings
articles.summary: The Saints must reverse a disturbing home trend in New Orleans and redeem a nightmare history with the Minnesota Vikings in Week 5.
articles.body:
Coming off an embarrassing Monday loss, the New Orleans Saints play their third straight home game when they host the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. The Saints lost both their first two games in the Superdome to fall to 1-3. It's the only time New Orleans has three straight home outings and one of only twice the Saints have consecutive home games this season. This will be the 39th meeting between the Saints and Vikings. Minnesota has a dominant advantage in this series, though there have been some memorable outcomes between the two.

Last meeting in New Orleans (2020): Saints (52-33)

Minnesota has a decided advantage in this series because of a couple stretches of dominance. The Saints actually won the first game in the series, a 20-17 victory at Tulane Stadium during the 1968 season. After that, the Vikings rattled off six straight wins over the Saints and won eight out of nine against them between 1970 and 1981. The only game that the Saints won over that stretch was a 31-28 victory at home to open the 1978 season in the first matchup between these teams in the Superdome.

Minnesota also defeated the Saints in four straight meetings between 1986 and 1990, actually taking eight of ten matchups between 1986 and 2001. Included in that span were two postseason victories. One of those was a 45-3 Vikings rout of the Saints inside the Superdome during the 1987-88 playoffs. It was the first postseason trip for the Saints. These teams are familiar postseason foes, having met five times in the playoffs.

New Orleans won only one of those playoff showdowns against the Vikings, but it was the one with the most on the line. The top-seeded Saints hosted the second-seeded Vikings in the 2010 NFC Championship game. It was billed as a showdown between Drew Brees and Brett Favre, two future Hall of Fame quarterbacks. The Saints were outgained in total yardage in the game but took advantage of five Minnesota turnovers. Brees led an overtime march for the game-winning field goal in a 31-28 win that propelled the Saints to a Super Bowl XLIV victory two weeks later. The Vikings have won the last two postseason matchups against the Saints, taking a miraculous 29-24 last second win in the 2018 divisional round and a 26-20 overtime victory in the 2020 wild-card round. The second of those were in the Superdome, giving the Vikings a 2-1 edge over the Saints in the playoffs in their own building.

Inside the Superdome, the Saints own a slim 8-6 all-time edge over Minnesota even including the playoffs. The most resounding of those was a 52-33 rout on Christmas Day in 2020. Alvin Kamara tied an NFL record that was set back in 1929 and unmatched since with six rushing touchdowns in the win. The last 'home' game for the Saints against the Vikings actually took place in London during the 2022 campaign. Minnesota won that by a 28-25 score on a last second field goal.

Prior to this matchup, the Saints and Vikings have faced off six times in the month of October. New Orleans is 3-3 in those matchups with five of them taking place at home, including three in the Superdome. However, the Vikings have won three of the last four times that they've played New Orleans in October. The Saints are now trying to get themselves right against a surprising 4-0 Minnesota squad. New Orleans has also lost 13 of their last 19 games played in the Superdome. To turn around their season, they need to reverse that trend on Sunday.

articles.title: Mizzou Receives Uplifting News About Freshman Johnnie Jones
articles.summary: The Missouri Tigers received disheartening news last week about their teammate Johnnie “DJ” Jones before the matchup with Florida. On Tuesday, Missouri head...
articles.body:
The Missouri Tigers received disheartening news last week about their teammate Johnnie "DJ" Jones before the matchup with Florida. On Tuesday, Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz shared with the media the reason that he shouted out Jones in his postgame interview following the big win.

During freshman intake, a heart issue was discovered, and the Tigers staff continued to monitor him for two weeks, but to no avail.

"We sent him to the Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville, Florida, and discovered a much more significant issue," Drinkwitz said on Tuesday. "And then last week we found out that Jonnie's now on a heart transplant list."

On Thursday morning, Drinkwitz posted a statement on X regarding the freshman offensive tackle.

Mizzou Freshman Johnnie Jones Received Heart Transplant

Thursday morning, Drinkwitz shared an uplifting update about Jones. "I have a great update to share on DJ," Drinkwitz posted to X . "Last night, DJ received his heart transplant, and his surgery went well. He is now recovering."

Drinkwitz was visibly choked up speaking about Jones on Tuesday, and asked the Mizzou family to keep Jones and his family in their prayers. "I know Johnnie was watching our game," Drinkwitz said. "It's just hard, an 18-year-old with everything in front of him, and you're just not prepared for that kind of news."

The Tigers got the news regarding their teammate last week and would go on to rout Florida in a statement win . Jones is now recovering. There is no knowledge of whether or not he would be able to suit up on the gridiron again, and currently that is not the most important thing in his recovery.

Mizzou Head Coach Eli Drinkwitz Grateful For Support

It has been a roller coaster of a week for the Missouri Tigers, and Eli Drinkwitz was the mouthpiece for the Jones family, the Missouri players, and the University regarding Jones.

"We are incredibly grateful for the medical team who cared for DJ and for the donor and donor family whose extraordinary gift made this possible," Drinkwitz said.

Mayo Clinic is a nationally acclaimed medical facility that took Jones in and discovered a more significant issue than the Tigers initially found.

In his post on X, Drinkwitz said, "Please continue to keep DJ, his family, the donor family, and his caregivers in your prayers as he begins the recovery process."

Drinkwitz also expressed thanks for the support from the fans, students, and alumni during this time. "We are so thankful for the incredible prayers and support from the entire Mizzou Family. We will continue to update you when we can," Drinkwitz posted.

Tiger fans can support by donating to the Jones Family's SupportNow as Jones begins a lengthy recovery process.

articles.title: Prosecutors in Maradona death trial seek sentences up to 12 years
articles.summary: Seven medical professionals face calls for 12-year prison sentences in trial over Argentina icon Diego Maradona’s death.
articles.body:
Argentine prosecutors argued on Thursday that the “chaotic” medical team treating football legend Diego Maradona at the time of his death should receive prison sentences of up to 12 years.

Seven medical professionals have been on trial since April over Maradona’s death on November 25, 2020 while convalescing after surgery for a brain clot.

The star of the 1986 World Cup died of heart failure and acute pulmonary edema – a condition where fluid accumulates in the lungs – at a rented home in the Buenos Aires suburb of Tigre two weeks after undergoing surgery.

The larger-than-life star, who had a history of substance abuse, was 60 at the time of his death.

His medical team, including his chief doctor, psychiatrist, psychologist and nurses, are accused of providing grossly inadequate care in the lead-up to his death. They deny the charges.

In his closing arguments, prosecutor Patricio Ferrai said the defendants’ “chaotic organisation” left the ailing patient “in a helpless situation, abandoning him to his fate”.

He accused them of having “breached their duties, performed actions contrary to the art of healing” and having “omitted all the acts they were required to perform”.

The defendants are charged with “dolo eventual” – a legal term meaning that a person is aware that their actions could cause harm but persisted nonetheless.

The highest prison sentence sought by prosecutors was 12 years, for Maradona’s personal physician, Leopoldo Luque.

Other sentences ranging from four to 10 years were sought for other medical staff, which include a psychiatrist, nurse and coordinators.

The health workers have argued that Maradona’s death could not have been foreseen and that they did their jobs. Each defendant has also downplayed their own individual responsibility for his care.

The case has revolved around whether the doctors’ decision to allow Maradona to convalesce in a private home, instead of in a hospital, was negligent.

The prosecution has also pointed to the near-total absence of medical equipment, such as a hospital bed, defibrillator or quickly available ambulance as evidence of what they presented as the defendants’ dereliction of duty.

Several medical experts testified that Maradona’s carers failed to react to key warning signs – he was suffering from edema, tachycardia and had difficulty breathing – in the lead-up to his death.

“Diego Armando Maradona’s death clearly did not come out of nowhere: the signs of this fatal outcome began to appear long beforehand,” assistant prosecutor Cosme Iribarren said on Thursday.

The prosecution again showed the court shocking images of the former footballer lying dead in bed, his stomach grotesquely swollen .

Maradona’s three daughters, who were present in court on Thursday for the start of the summation, covered their faces to avoid seeing the images.

The summation is expected to last around two weeks and the verdict is expected at a later date.

The first trial over Maradona’s death was dramatically annulled last year after two-and-a-half months of hearings, following revelations that one of the judges took part in a clandestine documentary about the case.

articles.title: How Hurricane Isaias could affect Sunday's Houston Texans-Tennessee Titans game in Nashville
articles.summary: The remnants of Hurricane Isaias currently are projected to blow through the Nashville area Sunday morning, hours before the Houston Texans play the Tennesse...
articles.body:
In their first game of the season in an true outdoor stadium, the Houston Texans may have to deal with some adverse weather conditions when they play the Tennessee Titans on Sunday in Nashville.

The noon kickoff at Nissan Stadium could be impacted by Hurricane Isaias , the first Atlantic hurricane of the season that is expected to make landfall near the Alabama-Florida border on Friday night.

Current track estimates have the storm heading north through Alabama and Mississippi on Saturday, which could impact that night's titanic college football tilt with No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Alabama in Tuscaloosa, and going through Nashville early Sunday morning. By that time, the intensity will have died down and will just be a depression, but still will impact Tennessee. The National Weather Service in Nashville reported Thursday morning that it expects the area to receive between 1-3 inches of rain and wind gusts up to 40 mph with the heaviest period of rain coming down Saturday night.

Sunday's forecast for Nashville calls for a rainy day with highs in the lower 70s with lows at about 60 degrees and rain chances dropping dramatically later in the evening.

The winless Texans are 0-3 playing under the closed roof of Reliant Stadium this season and their only road game - a loss at Indianapolis - was played with Lucas Oil Stadium's retractable roof open on a calm and sunny 70-degree day.

Playing under a constantly closed roof in Houston means the Texans rarely deal with rain on gamedays. They had a rough time in snowy conditions in last year's playoff loss at New England , and the last time they had to play at least partly through fairly heavy rain, they got trounced on the road by the New York Jets 30-6 in 2023.

articles.title: Progress is name of the game when it comes to the Raiders
articles.summary: A month into the regular season, and the Las Vegas Raiders can at least say that they are ahead of schedule.
articles.body:
A month into the regular season, and the Las Vegas Raiders can at least say that they are ahead of schedule.

A 3-1 record to start the year has the Raiders smashing expectations. Kirk Cousins has been the steady veteran presence at quarterback early on, while the defense has developed an identity as a unit unafraid to make plays on the ball. These have been driving forces for the Raiders so far, and a playoff berth no longer feels out of reach.

However, losing can provide some teachable moments and, in the event of the Raiders' loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, even a team that exceeding expectations is far from a finished product.

One of the major aspects of where the Raiders need work is developing a presence on the ground. Despite Klint Kubiak priding himself on establishing the run, the Raiders come into the Week Five slate of games last in the NFL with 3.1 yards per carry. The lack of consistency in the run game has served as the fly in the ointment for the Raiders offense, which still ranks eighth with 28.8 points per game and in the top half of the league with 343 yards per game.

Should the Raiders unlock the running game, the offensive execution will be able to closer reflect the ceiling of the talent it has at its disposal.

"I think we just have to pay attention to our details, starting with ourselves," said Raiders offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko on how to fix the run game.

"What we're asking of the players, what we are attacking each game plan and presenting a great plan to the players allowing them to be detailed so they can go out and play fast and attack it. That's what we look forward to doing."

Despite the issues, where the Raiders have succeeded is keeping Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington involved offensively, even when the results on the ground are not quite the best.

Jeanty has received some attention in the passing game, currently ranking second on the team with 19 receptions (tight end Michael Mayer leads with 20) and tied for the team lead with two touchdowns. Meanwhile, Washington has averaged five yards per carry so far, giving the Raiders the confidence needed to continue feeding the fourth-round rookie the ball and keep Jeanty fresh.

"[Mike's] a great player," said Jeanty about his rookie teammate. "He runs with a great mentality, so having him come in and the defense can't take a break, but I can take a break and catch my breath and come back in with fresh legs."

On defense, the Raiders still lead the league with nine takeaways and are still tied for fifth with 12 sacks, but the Chiefs also provided some film to learn from.

The Chiefs were able to generate explosive plays against the Raiders and, while part of that does come simply due to the level of talent in Kansas City's offense, first-year defensive coordinator Rob Leonard still has some moments he can look into to continue tightening up defensively. Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes was also able to get some time to work against the young defensive backs on the Raiders such as Hezekiah Masses and Treydan Stukes, so converting pressure into sacks and disrupting offensive rhythm is also something the Raiders can key in on.

"I'm happy with the progression in the process that we're chasing and chipping away at every day throughout the week and focusing on getting better and fixing problems and communication," said Leonard.

"I think we've consistently got better and, through each game, there are things that we have to fix and, as long as we're honest about those things, it's been good."

The Raiders have done everything in their power to push themselves into respectability. It is now a matter of honing everything else so they can continue their success into December and beyond.
